statement: You are given an integer n. Return true if n equals 2ˣ for some integer x ≥ 0, and false otherwise.
A positive power of two has exactly one 1 bit. Subtracting 1 turns that bit off and every lower bit on, so for n > 0 the test n & (n − 1) == 0 is true exactly when n is a power of two.

examples.explanation: 16 is 10000 and 15 is 01111. They share no bits, so 16 & 15 = 0 and 16 is a power of two.
18 is 10010 and 17 is 10001. Bit 4 survives the AND, so 18 & 17 = 16, which is not 0.
1 = 2⁰. It has a single 1 bit, and 1 & 0 = 0.
